title: Understanding the Components
text: The expected squared error can be broken down into three main components: variance, bias squared, and irreducible error. Can you identify which part of the equation represents each of these components?

title: Focus on Variance
text: Consider the term E[(E[f_hat_theta(x)]-f_hat_theta(x))**2]. This term is related to the variability of the model predictions around their expected value. What does this tell you about the model's variance?

title: Identifying the Irreducible Error
text: Which term in the equation represents the irreducible error, which is the noise inherent in the data that cannot be reduced by any model?

title: Exploring Bias
text: The term (h(x)-E[f_hat_theta(x)])**2 represents the bias squared. This term measures the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. How does this affect the model's predictions?
